keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Medical image analysis
keywords.about: MRI-based diagnosis and lesion segmentation for clinical decision support.

keywords.name: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
keywords.about: Adapters and LoRA variants adapt large models cheaply, including with missing modalities.

keywords.name: Video grounding and captioning
keywords.about: Locating moments in video and captioning them under weak or clinical supervision.

keywords.name: Vision-language models
keywords.about: Frozen and adapted VLMs are probed for test-time adaptation, abstention and edge deployment.

keywords.name: Object detection
keywords.about: Detectors for small objects and adverse weather, including spiking and YOLO designs.

keywords.name: LLM agents
keywords.about: Coding agents gain memory management, backdoor analysis, proof repair and multi-agent coordination.

keywords.name: FPS
keywords.about: Models are built for fast on-device inference, trading accuracy for throughput.

keywords.name: Vector sketching
keywords.about: Training-free vector sketch generation and outpainting with stroke-level structure and style control.

keywords.name: Visual question answering
keywords.about: Medical and scientific VQA improves through retrieval, in-context learning and self-improvement.

keywords.name: Computational pathology
keywords.about: Stain normalization and open pathology foundation models close cross-hospital generalization gaps.

keywords.name: Plant disease detection
keywords.about: Ontology-based and bias-mitigated vision models recognize plant and fruit disease.

themes.name: Medical image analysis and clinical AI
themes.summary: The papers develop clinical AI and medical image analysis methods spanning neuroimaging, pathology, radiology, dental imaging, echocardiography, and surgical video. They differ by focusing on data integration and annotation, segmentation and grounding, generative or synthetic imaging, cross-site robustness, and explainability or deployment safeguards.

themes.name: Efficient edge vision and model compression
themes.summary: The papers make vision and multimodal models practical on resource-constrained edge hardware by pruning redundant blocks or tokens, compressing weights, designing lightweight detectors and accelerators, and reducing inference energy and memory traffic. They differ in which bottleneck they target, from model redundancy and arithmetic precision to hardware dataflow, visual-token and KV-cache cost, and deployment robustness.

themes.name: Geospatial remote sensing and environmental mapping
themes.summary: The papers apply deep learning and geospatial foundation models to remote-sensing and environmental mapping tasks, including small-object detection, permafrost thaw mapping, species distribution modeling, geolocalization, and urban building analysis. They differ in target phenomenon, data modality, and emphasis on detection, segmentation, retrieval, or benchmark auditing.

themes.name: LLM agents and autonomous code generation
themes.summary: These papers develop and evaluate LLM agents for long-horizon work, with several focusing on memory/context selection, multi-agent coordination in shared codebases, and autonomous generation or repair of code and formal proofs. Others examine agent security, GUI interaction, CAD generation, and multi-party collaboration, differing by whether they contribute systems, benchmarks, or empirical studies.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning for robot control
themes.summary: The papers develop reinforcement-learning methods and evaluation tools for robot control, spanning new decision-process formulations, benchmarks, certification, and lifelong or humanoid embodied learning. They differ in focus: some propose algorithms and safety guarantees, some build benchmarks and interpretability or dialogue-driven skill learning, and others apply autonomy to manipulation, surgery, and planning.

themes.name: Video temporal grounding and world modeling
themes.summary: The papers study how video models forecast, localize, and reason about temporal events and scene evolution. Some learn evolving concept states, object relations, or sparse latent dynamics for forecasting and counterfactual world modeling, while others improve temporal grounding, action recognition, captioning, streaming translation, and reaction understanding through adapters, cross-conditioning, reinforcement learning, and structured generation. They differ in whether they predict future states, localize language-described events, edit interactions, or synthesize viewpoint-transformed video.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow matching generative models
themes.summary: The papers apply diffusion, flow matching, and related generative priors to a wide range of tasks: Riemannian flow matching for InSAR phase denoising, a scale-free-attention diffusion transformer for image generation, flow-matching priors for Fourier phase retrieval, implicit denoiser priors for linear inverse problems, normalizing flows for calorimeter anomaly detection, training-free vector sketching, a theory of model collapse in iterative Gaussian estimation, and physics-grounded video generation. They differ in domain and in whether they build new generative architectures, reuse pretrained priors as regularizers, or analyze generative training dynamics theoretically.

themes.name: Vision-language model adaptation and robustness
themes.summary: The papers examine how vision-language models can be adapted, evaluated, and made more robust, spanning test-time adaptation, selective prediction, CLIP fine-tuning diagnostics, self-improvement, referential grounding, audio-language conflict, semantic correspondence, and omnimodal embeddings. They differ in whether they propose new scoring or decoding procedures, analyze confidence and forgetting signals, generate synthetic practice data, or build benchmarks and surveys. Together they highlight adaptation gains alongside risks such as uneven abstention, transfer degradation, and conflict between modalities.

themes.name: Graph and structured representation learning
themes.summary: The papers use graph and structured representations to improve robustness, interpretability, calibration, evaluation, or efficiency across physiological, neuroimaging, query, embedding, temporal, and logic tasks. They differ in whether the graph encodes detector candidates, brain topology, provenance dependencies, node descriptors, embedding neighborhoods, temporal experts, or logic circuits, and in whether the goal is prediction, calibration, fidelity measurement, or classification.

themes.name: Fairness privacy and trustworthy auditing
themes.summary: The papers investigate fairness, privacy, and trustworthiness through empirical audits, mitigation methods, and participatory assessments. They cover age gaps in facial expression recognition, background bias in plant disease detection, privacy effects on generative-model fairness, sensitive-attribute erasure, transformer counterfactual fairness, AI-agent failure modes, and community-based harm auditing. Their approaches differ as empirical evaluations, representation-learning interventions, and bottom-up or participatory auditing frameworks.

themes.name: AI-generated content detection and watermarking
themes.summary: The papers develop methods for detecting AI-generated or manipulated visual content and for protecting generated content through watermarking. They differ in technical focus: aggregating intermediate encoder representations and whitening residuals for image detection, adaptive margin control for diffusion watermarking, quality-based morphing attack detection, and evaluating prompt stealing and fidelity failures in generated video.

themes.name: OCR document and scientific figure understanding
themes.summary: The papers focus on extracting, parsing, verifying, and evaluating information from documents, charts, diagrams, and scientific figures. They differ in their emphasis on statistical-visual verification for exploratory data analysis, data-centric OCR for low-resource scripts, benchmarked structural recovery of historical diagrams, vision-language document parsing, line-chart simplification assessment, and retrieval-augmented scientific visual question answering.

highlights.title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation
highlights.authors: Zixuan Huang, Tianhao You, Guozhang Chen   School of Computer Science et al.
highlights.theme: Diffusion and flow matching generative models
highlights.why: Scale-Free Attention yields O(N log N) diffusion transformers with massive speedups and improved FID over full attention, making high-resolution generation significantly more efficient.
highlights.key_result: SFA achieves the best generation quality among five attention mechanisms, including full attention, after 40 epochs of PixelFlow training from scratch on ImageNet at 256 256 resolution, reaching the lowest FID of 12.51; its Triton implementation also achieves 357.3 forward and 265.6 backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens.
evidence: Our Triton implementation achieves 357.3 forward and 265.6 backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens.
After 40 epochs of PixelFlow training from scratch on ImageNet at 256 256 resolution, SFA achieves the best generation quality among five attention mechanisms, including full attention.
At 40 epochs, SFA achieves the lowest FID of 12.51 and the highest IS of 101.20 among the five attention mechanisms.

highlights.title: Exact Dice Degradation Envelopes for Label-Free Segmentation Update Selection
highlights.theme: Medical image analysis and clinical AI
highlights.why: Provides an exact deterministic bound on Dice degradation for label-free segmentation updates, with exhaustive validation, offering a strong safety guarantee for clinical deployment.
highlights.key_result: We derive the exact largest decrease in binary Dice between a baseline and a candidate, maximized over every possible unknown reference mask on the same pixels. Exhaustive and randomized validation checks 5,026,592 reference masks with no discrepancy.
evidence: We derive the exact largest decrease in binary Dice between a baseline and a candidate, maximized over every possible unknown reference mask on the same pixels. A maximizing reference always lies inside baseline foreground: three observable mask counts reduce the problem to at most four reference-cardinality checks.
A finite grid of logit interpolations permits partial candidate outputs without extra network forwards. Exhaustive and randomized validation checks 5,026,592 reference masks with no discrepancy.

highlights.title: FORCE: Factorized Object Relations for Counterfactual Editing in Video World Models
highlights.theme: Video temporal grounding and world modeling
highlights.why: FORCE enables explicit, persistent counterfactual edits of pairwise object relations in video world models, validated against simulator responses, advancing interpretable world modeling.
highlights.key_result: On held-out clips, FORCE's edits made from video agree with the simulator's response at 0.19 to 0.37 on our effect-based score; trained and scored on exact object positions instead, the same architecture reaches 0.57 to 0.85. The gap therefore lies not in the learned relational dynamics but in perception: what bounds an edit is how precisely objects can be located from video, and the precision editing needs lies just beyond what current object-centric perception delivers.

highlights.title: Diagnosing Zero-Shot Forgetting in CLIP Fine-Tuning: Attention Drift Characterizes Adaptation, Representation Drift Predicts Transfer Degradation
highlights.why: Identifies CKA representation drift as a strong predictor of zero-shot forgetting during CLIP fine-tuning, enabling prediction without labeled transfer benchmarks.
highlights.key_result: CKA ranks runs by retention at =0.960, and the ranking is already established after the first of six epochs ( =0.959). Within a fixed configuration, the change in attention entropy is strongly associated with forgetting (mean | |=0.860).

highlights.title: SparseWAM: Driving World-Action Models are Worth 16 Register Tokens
highlights.authors: Yixiang Yang, Lizhong Zhang, Xingyu Zhang et al.
highlights.theme: Video temporal grounding and world modeling
highlights.why: SparseWAM compresses driving world-action models to 16 register tokens, retaining imagine-then-act reasoning and achieving strong NAVSIM scores at low latency.
highlights.key_result: As a result, our SparseWAM achieves 92.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 39.6 on NavHard at only 164 ms latency, roughly 1/5 that of DriveVA, demonstrating the efficiency of the sparse register space.
evidence: As a result, our SparseWAM achieves 92.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 39.6 on NavHard at only 164 ms latency, roughly 1/5 that of DriveVA, demonstrating the efficiency of the sparse register space.

highlights.title: OpenMidnight: Closing the Performance Gap Between Open and Proprietary Pathology Foundation Models
highlights.authors: Ratna Sagari Grandhi, Anis Chihoub, Ryan Kim et al.
highlights.theme: Medical image analysis and clinical AI
highlights.why: OpenMidnight provides an open-source pathology foundation model that matches or exceeds proprietary models on THUNDER while using 34x less compute.
highlights.key_result: OpenMidnight 1.1 is an open-source replication and refinement of Midnight trained on approximately 12,000 publicly available whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas and uses approximately 320 H100 GPU-hours for pathology pretraining---a 34-fold reduction relative to the compute reported for Midnight. Across 16 classification and four segmentation datasets in THUNDER, it achieves the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models, ahead of Midnight.
evidence: We present OpenMidnight 1.1, an open-source replication and refinement of Midnight trained on approximately 12,000 publicly available whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas.

Using an encoder initialized with pretrained DINOv2 weights, OpenMidnight 1.1 uses approximately 320 H100 GPU-hours for pathology pretraining---a 34-fold reduction relative to the compute reported for Midnight.

Across 16 classification and four segmentation datasets in THUNDER, OpenMidnight 1.1 achieves the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models, ahead of Midnight, with performance that matches or exceeds models trained on substantially larger datasets in several tasks.

highlights.title: AegisBench: Auditing Aerial Search-and-Rescue Person Detection Under the Conditions It Is Deployed In
highlights.theme: Geospatial remote sensing and environmental mapping
highlights.why: AegisBench reveals catastrophic failure of aerial person detectors under disaster conditions like low light, an important deployment robustness audit.
highlights.key_result: Low light is the extreme case: a 4.5-stop exposure loss drives recall to exactly zero for all three detectors on both datasets, a result that holds under threshold-free mAP and across three training seeds, and is mirrored on 300 real night drone images, where 2 of 759 people are found.
evidence: Low light is the extreme case: a 4.5-stop exposure loss drives recall to exactly zero for all three detectors on both datasets, a result that holds under threshold-free mAP and across three training seeds, and is mirrored on 300 real night drone images, where 2 of 759 people are found.

highlights.title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents
highlights.authors: Georgios Syros, Blake Bullwinkel, Alina Oprea et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agents and autonomous code generation
highlights.why: Kerkoporta shows structured-output backdoors in coding agents achieve up to 96.2% attack success while preserving utility, extending serious security risks to agentic settings.
highlights.key_result: Kerkoporta, a two-stage poisoning pipeline that implants structured-output backdoors in reasoning coding agents, "reaches success rates of up to 96.2% and can be configured to generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target," while the resulting models "can outperform the clean baseline on standard utility benchmarks."
evidence: We introduce structured-output backdoor attacks against reasoning models in agentic coding settings. A trigger placed anywhere in the agent's context causes the model to emit an attacker-chosen tool call, which the harness executes, directly compromising the system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

The attack reaches success rates of up to 96.2% and can be configured to generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target. The resulting models can outperform the clean baseline on standard utility benchmarks, giving victims a direct incentive to adopt them.

We evaluate our methodology across 2 open-weight LLMs, 3 state-of-the-art coding harnesses, and 3 attacker payloads that compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the user, reaching attack success rates of up to 96.2% while maintaining clean task performance.

news.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI describes Pando, a new backend for Git repositories that powers its monorepo and is designed for horizontally scalable writes to many branches and high read throughput, while staying compatible with the Git protocol and client. In production it cut median push latency by nearly 5x and delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day; before this, reliability at times fell below 90%.

news.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
news.summary: OpenAI launched the Grid Protectors Program, a national effort to work with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for future compute campuses to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain. For its planned Effingham County campus, the agreement with Georgia Power includes up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response, which the post says equals the average demand of roughly 700,000 households, against projected U.S. data center capacity exceeding 100 gigawatts by 2030.

news.title: LifeVal
news.summary: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, an evaluation of everyday tasks drawn from the American Time Use Survey and Multinational Time Use Study plus a new demographically representative survey of 3,995 respondents, covering areas such as caregiving, health, education, personal finances and government services. OpenAI says it used the evaluation over the past year to track and drive model improvement on such tasks.

news.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
news.summary: Google recap of October 2026 AI announcements: Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier reasoning model, rolled out globally across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Search and the Gemini app, and Gemini 4 Carbon was announced two weeks later and is in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program. The post also lists Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio and a global English rollout of SynthID Detector, after watermarking more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

news.title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution
news.summary: NVIDIA released NVIDIA Attribution, an open-source tool that correlates workload-scoped logs, metrics, telemetry and scheduler state into a structured diagnosis with outcome, root cause, affected nodes, symptoms and evidence trail, deployed as a REST-API Service plus a Python Blueprint with connectors for Slurm, Kueue, Loki, local files, Kubernetes pod logs and PromQL. NVIDIA says it is used in production across its AI infrastructure, analyzing millions of workloads weekly across hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

news.title: Keep Distributed Training Running with Automated Workload Recovery
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Recovery, an open-source workload-level service that automates a four-stage recovery loop (detect, attribute, isolate, restart or stop by policy) across cluster training jobs, integrated with Slurm via a Helm-deployed Advisor Controller and defaulting to monitor mode with a persistent audit trail. Production monitoring on one training cluster from July 9 to October 9 covered nearly 200 jobs per day and recorded about 8,550 anomaly detections, with mean detection and recovery-action latencies of 69 and 94 seconds.

news.title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One
news.summary: NVIDIA described AICR (AI Cluster Runtime), which captures tuned Kubernetes configurations as recipes, generates deployment bundles and validates running clusters for Vera Rubin NVL72, with a recipe specifying the R615.23 open kernel driver, DRA driver v0.5.0 with ComputeDomains and Ubuntu 26.04 with a 64k-page kernel. Validation with GPU Operator v26.7.0 passed deployment, conformance and a cross-node NCCL all-reduce gate at 744.71 GB/s bus bandwidth at 16 GiB, and early-silicon testing surfaced an unmapped Rubin architecture value in go-nvlib that crash-looped the DRA kubelet plugin, fixed in the v0.5.0 release.

news.title: Build World Models for Interactive Simulation with NVIDIA Cosmos
news.summary: NVIDIA described Cosmos, a platform of world foundation models and development tools, including the open modular Cosmos Framework for training, RL (DPO, GRPO, PPO, OPD, DiffusionNFT), optimization and inference across Cosmos 3, Alpamayo, GR00T, Qwen and pi0.5, plus Cosmos NIM microservices. NIM serving with quantization, speculative decoding and KV-cache-aware routing gives roughly 2–3x speedups on H200 GPUs, and Cosmos3-Nano generation needs 58 GiB in BF16 and 44 GiB in FP8 with offloading.

news.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI
news.summary: AWS describes preparing web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI, an open-source Python crawler that writes Markdown and a metadata sidecar per page to Amazon S3 for ingestion through an S3 data source. The post positions this batch preparation path for cases needing main-content extraction, CSS-selector-scoped extraction or custom metadata, distinct from real-time web access at inference time such as Web Grounding with Amazon Nova.

news.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
news.summary: AWS describes using sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) on Amazon SageMaker AI to fine-tune a smaller student shopping agent on multi-step trajectories generated by a frontier teacher, then evaluate it against a held-out benchmark. The post notes SeqKD needs only the teacher's text outputs, with no logits or reinforcement-learning infrastructure.

news.title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS describes a multi-agent engineering assistant for aerospace part substitution evaluation built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, with a planner (Claude Haiku 5.5) routing to Catalog, Evaluation and Knowledge specialists (Claude Sonnet 5.5), a supervisor (Claude Opus 5.5), and deterministic Python tolerance-rule scoring. Retrieval uses Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and an S3 Vectors index, and every evaluation writes an audit trail entry aligned with AS9100 sections 8.4 and 8.5.6, with the engineer making all substitution decisions.

news.title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Circle K built an automated DevOps incident triage system on Amazon Bedrock, first with Amazon Bedrock Flows and later migrated to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, that investigates each alert and posts a structured summary to Slack. Since deployment, mean triage time fell to under 15 minutes, a 67–75 percent reduction, at a company operating more than 17,200 stores across 27 countries where manual triage previously took 45–60 minutes.

themes.name: 高效边缘视觉与模型压缩

themes.name: 地理空间遥感与环境制图

themes.name: LLM 智能体与自主代码生成

themes.name: 用于机器人控制的强化学习

themes.name: 视频时序定位与世界模型
themes.summary: 这些论文研究视频模型如何预测、定位和推理时序事件及场景演变。一些论文学习演化的概念状态、物体关系或稀疏潜在动态，用于预测和反事实世界建模；另一些论文通过适配器、交叉条件、强化学习和结构化生成改进时序定位、动作识别、字幕生成、流式翻译和反应理解。它们的区别在于预测未来状态、定位语言描述的事件、编辑交互或合成视角变换视频。

themes.name: 扩散与流匹配生成模型

themes.name: 视觉语言模型适配与鲁棒性

themes.name: 图与结构化表示学习

themes.name: 公平性隐私与可信审计

themes.name: AI 生成内容检测与数字水印

themes.name: OCR 文档与科学图表理解

highlights.title: SFA: A Statistical Physics-Inspired Diffusion Transformer for Efficient and High-Quality Image Generation
highlights.authors: Zixuan Huang, Tianhao You, Guozhang Chen   School of Computer Science et al.
highlights.theme: Diffusion and flow matching generative models
highlights.why: Scale-Free Attention 带来了 O(N log N) 复杂度的扩散 Transformer，相比 full attention 具有大幅加速和更优的 FID，使高分辨率生成显著更高效。
highlights.key_result: SFA 在 ImageNet 256 256 分辨率上从头训练 PixelFlow 40 个 epoch 后，在包括 full attention 在内的五种注意力机制中取得了最佳生成质量，达到最低的 FID 12.51；其 Triton 实现在 262,144 个 token 上相对于 FlashAttention 还获得了 357.3 倍前向和 265.6 倍后向注意力加速。
evidence: Our Triton implementation achieves 357.3 forward and 265.6 backward attention speedups over FlashAttention at 262,144 tokens.
After 40 epochs of PixelFlow training from scratch on ImageNet at 256 256 resolution, SFA achieves the best generation quality among five attention mechanisms, including full attention.
At 40 epochs, SFA achieves the lowest FID of 12.51 and the highest IS of 101.20 among the five attention mechanisms.

highlights.title: Exact Dice Degradation Envelopes for Label-Free Segmentation Update Selection
highlights.theme: Medical image analysis and clinical AI
highlights.why: 为无标签分割更新提供了 Dice 退化的精确确定性边界，并经过穷举验证，为临床部署提供了强有力的安全保障。
highlights.key_result: 我们推导出在相同像素上对所有可能未知参考掩码最大化时，二值 Dice 在基线和候选之间的精确最大下降量。穷举和随机验证检查了 5,026,592 个参考掩码，无任何差异。
evidence: We derive the exact largest decrease in binary Dice between a baseline and a candidate, maximized over every possible unknown reference mask on the same pixels. A maximizing reference always lies inside baseline foreground: three observable mask counts reduce the problem to at most four reference-cardinality checks.
A finite grid of logit interpolations permits partial candidate outputs without extra network forwards. Exhaustive and randomized validation checks 5,026,592 reference masks with no discrepancy.

highlights.title: FORCE: Factorized Object Relations for Counterfactual Editing in Video World Models
highlights.theme: Video temporal grounding and world modeling
highlights.why: FORCE 支持在视频世界模型中对成对物体关系进行显式、持久的反事实编辑，并通过模拟器响应进行验证，推进可解释的世界建模。
highlights.key_result: 在留出视频片段上，FORCE 基于视频生成的编辑与我们基于效果的分数上模拟器的响应一致程度为 0.19 到 0.37；改为在精确物体位置上训练和评分时，相同架构达到 0.57 到 0.85。因此差距不在于学习到的关系动态，而在于感知：编辑受限于从视频中定位物体的精确度，而编辑所需的精确度恰恰超出了当前以物体为中心的感知所能提供的水平。
evidence: On held-out clips, FORCE's edits made from video agree with the simulator's response at 0.19 to 0.37 on our effect-based score; trained and scored on exact object positions instead, the same architecture reaches 0.57 to 0.85.

The gap therefore lies not in the learned relational dynamics but in perception: what bounds an edit is how precisely objects can be located from video, and the precision editing needs lies just beyond what current object-centric perception delivers.

highlights.title: Diagnosing Zero-Shot Forgetting in CLIP Fine-Tuning: Attention Drift Characterizes Adaptation, Representation Drift Predicts Transfer Degradation
highlights.why: 将 CKA 表示漂移识别为 CLIP 微调期间零样本遗忘的强预测因子，从而无需带标注的迁移基准即可进行预测。
highlights.key_result: CKA 在保留率 =0.960 时对运行进行排名，且该排名在六个 epoch 中的第一个之后已经确立（=0.959）。在固定配置下，注意力熵的变化与遗忘强相关（平均 | |=0.860）。
evidence: CKA ranks runs by retention at =0.960, and the ranking is already established after the first of six epochs ( =0.959).
Within a fixed configuration, the change in attention entropy is strongly associated with forgetting (mean | |=0.860).

highlights.title: SparseWAM: Driving World-Action Models are Worth 16 Register Tokens
highlights.authors: Yixiang Yang, Lizhong Zhang, Xingyu Zhang et al.
highlights.theme: Video temporal grounding and world modeling
highlights.why: SparseWAM 将驾驶世界-动作模型压缩到 16 个寄存器 token，保留先想象后行动的推理能力，并在低延迟下取得强劲的 NAVSIM 分数。
highlights.key_result: 因此，我们的 SparseWAM 在 NAVSIM v1 上达到 92.6 PDMS，在 NAVSIM v2 上达到 90.1 EPDMS，在 NavHard 上达到 39.6，延迟仅 164 ms，约为 DriveVA 的 1/5，展示了稀疏寄存器空间的高效性。
evidence: As a result, our SparseWAM achieves 92.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 39.6 on NavHard at only 164 ms latency, roughly 1/5 that of DriveVA, demonstrating the efficiency of the sparse register space.

highlights.title: OpenMidnight: Closing the Performance Gap Between Open and Proprietary Pathology Foundation Models
highlights.authors: Ratna Sagari Grandhi, Anis Chihoub, Ryan Kim et al.
highlights.theme: Medical image analysis and clinical AI
highlights.why: OpenMidnight 提供了一个开源病理基础模型，在 THUNDER 上达到或超过专有模型，同时使用的算力减少 34x。
highlights.key_result: OpenMidnight 1.1 is an open-source replication and refinement of Midnight trained on approximately 12,000 publicly available whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas and uses approximately 320 H100 GPU-hours for pathology pretraining---a 34-fold reduction relative to the compute reported for Midnight. Across 16 classification and four segmentation datasets in THUNDER, it achieves the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models, ahead of Midnight.
evidence: We present OpenMidnight 1.1, an open-source replication and refinement of Midnight trained on approximately 12,000 publicly available whole-slide images from The Cancer Genome Atlas.

Using an encoder initialized with pretrained DINOv2 weights, OpenMidnight 1.1 uses approximately 320 H100 GPU-hours for pathology pretraining---a 34-fold reduction relative to the compute reported for Midnight.

Across 16 classification and four segmentation datasets in THUNDER, OpenMidnight 1.1 achieves the highest mean segmentation Dice (69.7) and ranks fourth among 14 models, ahead of Midnight, with performance that matches or exceeds models trained on substantially larger datasets in several tasks.

highlights.title: AegisBench: Auditing Aerial Search-and-Rescue Person Detection Under the Conditions It Is Deployed In
highlights.theme: Geospatial remote sensing and environmental mapping
highlights.why: AegisBench 揭示了低光照等灾害条件下航拍行人检测器的灾难性失效，这是一项重要的部署鲁棒性审计。
highlights.key_result: 低光照是极端情况：4.5-stop 的曝光损失使三个检测器在两个数据集上的召回率都恰好降为零，这一结果在无阈值 mAP 和三个训练种子下均成立，并在 300 张真实夜间无人机图像中得到印证，其中 759 人中仅发现 2 人。
evidence: Low light is the extreme case: a 4.5-stop exposure loss drives recall to exactly zero for all three detectors on both datasets, a result that holds under threshold-free mAP and across three training seeds, and is mirrored on 300 real night drone images, where 2 of 759 people are found.

highlights.title: Kerkoporta: Injecting Structured-Output Backdoors in Reasoning Coding Agents
highlights.authors: Georgios Syros, Blake Bullwinkel, Alina Oprea et al.
highlights.theme: LLM agents and autonomous code generation
highlights.why: Kerkoporta 表明编码智能体中的结构化输出后门可在保持效用的同时实现高达 96.2% 的攻击成功率，将严重安全风险扩展到智能体场景。
highlights.key_result: Kerkoporta 是一个两阶段投毒流水线，向推理编码智能体中植入结构化输出后门，"成功率高达 96.2%，并可配置为跨测试框架泛化或绑定到单一目标"，同时生成的模型"在标准效用基准上可优于干净基线"。
evidence: We introduce structured-output backdoor attacks against reasoning models in agentic coding settings. A trigger placed anywhere in the agent's context causes the model to emit an attacker-chosen tool call, which the harness executes, directly compromising the system's confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

The attack reaches success rates of up to 96.2% and can be configured to generalize across harnesses or bind to a single target. The resulting models can outperform the clean baseline on standard utility benchmarks, giving victims a direct incentive to adopt them.

We evaluate our methodology across 2 open-weight LLMs, 3 state-of-the-art coding harnesses, and 3 attacker payloads that compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the user, reaching attack success rates of up to 96.2% while maintaining clean task performance.

news.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI 介绍了 Pando，一种用于 Git 仓库的新后端，为其 monorepo 提供动力，设计用于水平扩展对多分支的写入和高读取吞吐量，同时保持与 Git 协议和客户端的兼容性。在生产环境中，它将中位推送延迟降低了近 5x，每天交付近一个 petabyte 的 Git 数据；在此之前，可靠性有时低于 90%。

news.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
news.summary: OpenAI 启动了 Grid Protectors Program，这是一项全国性行动，与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，为未来的计算园区制定安排，以便在电网紧张时降低电力需求。对于其计划中的 Effingham County 园区，与 Georgia Power 的协议包括高达 1,000 megawatts 的灵活需求响应，据该帖子称这相当于约 700,000 户家庭的平均需求，而预计到 2030 年美国数据中心容量将超过 100 gigawatts。

news.title: LifeVal
news.summary: OpenAI 推出了 LifeVal，这是一项基于 American Time Use Survey 和 Multinational Time Use Study 以及一项新的具有人口统计学代表性的 3,995 名受访者调查的日常任务评估，涵盖照护、健康、教育、个人财务和政府服务等领域。OpenAI 表示在过去一年中使用该评估来跟踪并推动模型在这些任务上的改进。

news.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
news.summary: Google recap of October 2026 AI announcements: Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier reasoning model, rolled out globally across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Google Cloud, Search and the Gemini app, and Gemini 4 Carbon was announced two weeks later and is in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program. The post also lists Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio and a global English rollout of SynthID Detector, after watermarking more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

news.title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution
news.summary: NVIDIA 发布了 NVIDIA Attribution，这是一款开源工具，将工作负载范围内的日志、指标、遥测数据和调度器状态关联为结构化诊断，包含结果、根本原因、受影响节点、症状和证据链，以 REST-API 服务加 Python Blueprint 的形式部署，并提供 Slurm、Kueue、Loki、本地文件、Kubernetes pod 日志和 PromQL 的连接器。NVIDIA 表示该工具已在其 AI 基础设施的生产环境中使用，每周分析数百万个工作负载，覆盖数十万个 GPU。

news.title: Keep Distributed Training Running with Automated Workload Recovery
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Recovery, an open-source workload-level service that automates a four-stage recovery loop (detect, attribute, isolate, restart or stop by policy) across cluster training jobs, integrated with Slurm via a Helm-deployed Advisor Controller and defaulting to monitor mode with a persistent audit trail. Production monitoring on one training cluster from July 9 to October 9 covered nearly 200 jobs per day and recorded about 8,550 anomaly detections, with mean detection and recovery-action latencies of 69 and 94 seconds.

news.title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One
news.summary: NVIDIA 描述了 AICR（AI Cluster Runtime），它将调优后的 Kubernetes 配置捕获为 recipe，生成部署包，并为 Vera Rubin NVL72 验证运行中的集群，其中一个 recipe 指定了 R615.23 开源内核驱动、带 ComputeDomains 的 DRA 驱动 v0.5.0，以及使用 64k-page 内核的 Ubuntu 26.04。使用 GPU Operator v26.7.0 进行的验证通过了部署、一致性检查以及跨节点 NCCL all-reduce 门控测试，在 16 GiB 下总线带宽达到 744.71 GB/s；早期硅片测试发现 go-nvlib 中一个未映射的 Rubin 架构值导致 DRA kubelet 插件崩溃循环，该问题已在 v0.5.0 版本中修复。

news.title: Build World Models for Interactive Simulation with NVIDIA Cosmos
news.summary: NVIDIA 描述了 Cosmos，这是一个世界基础模型和开发工具平台，包括开放的模块化 Cosmos Framework，用于训练、RL（DPO、GRPO、PPO、OPD、DiffusionNFT）、优化和推理，支持 Cosmos 3、Alpamayo、GR00T、Qwen 和 pi0.5，以及 Cosmos NIM 微服务。NIM 服务结合量化、投机解码和 KV-cache 感知路由，在 H200 GPU 上实现约 2–3x 加速；Cosmos3-Nano 生成在 BF16 下需要 58 GiB，在 FP8 下配合 offloading 需要 44 GiB。

news.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI
news.summary: AWS 描述了使用 Crawl4AI 为 Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases 准备 Web 内容，Crawl4AI 是一个开源 Python 爬虫，为每个页面将 Markdown 和元数据 sidecar 写入 Amazon S3，以便通过 S3 数据源进行摄取。该帖子将这种批量准备路径定位为适用于需要提取正文、限定 CSS 选择器的提取或自定义元数据的场景，与推理时的实时 Web 访问（如使用 Amazon Nova 的 Web Grounding）不同。

news.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
news.summary: AWS 描述了在 Amazon SageMaker AI 上使用序列级知识蒸馏（SeqKD）对基于前沿教师模型生成的多步轨迹微调一个更小的学生购物智能体，然后将其与留出基准进行评估。该帖子指出 SeqKD 仅需要教师的文本输出，无需 logits 或强化学习基础设施。

news.title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS 描述了基于 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 和 Strands Agents SDK 构建的航空航天零件替换评估多智能体工程助手，其中一个 planner（Claude Haiku 5.5）将任务路由到 Catalog、Evaluation 和 Knowledge 专家（Claude Sonnet 5.5），一个 supervisor（Claude Opus 5.5），以及确定性的 Python 公差规则评分。检索使用 Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases 配合 Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings 和 S3 Vectors 索引，每次评估都会写入一条与 AS9100 第 8.4 和 8.5.6 节对齐的审计跟踪记录，所有替换决定由工程师做出。

news.title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Circle K 在 Amazon Bedrock 上构建了一个自动化 DevOps 事件分类系统，最初使用 Amazon Bedrock Flows，后来迁移到 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore，该系统调查每条警报并将结构化摘要发布到 Slack。自部署以来，平均分类时间降至 15 分钟以下，减少了 67–75 percent，该公司在 27 个国家经营超过 17,200 家门店，此前人工分类耗时 45–60 分钟。
